newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN JULY YR/YR INFLATION HIGHEST SINCE JUNE '95.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN JULY YR/YR INFLATION HIGHEST SINCE JUNE '95.

text.p: German inflation rose to 1.9 percent year-on-year in July, its highest rate since June 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said on Tuesday.
The month-on-month rise in the consumer price index was 0.5 percent, the highest since January 1997. In June, the increases were 1.7 percent and 0.2 percent respectively.
The figures back up a warning last week by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing that prices were moving "in the wrong direction".
Issing's remarks may have been a hint that the central bank could begin to nudge interest rates higher to combat inflation and the weak mark.
The Statistics Office said one of the main reasons for the relatively strong increase in prices was a rise in the share of the cost of medicines that consumers must pay.
Without that increase, consumer prices would have been only 0.3 percent higher than in June, it said.
Fish and coffee prices also rose strongly, while fresh vegetables, fruit and flowers fell, it said.
